precepts.text: A lot of times we desire things but do not receive them because we do not ask; ye have not because ye ask not.
precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

precepts.why:
“Attend unto my cry; for I am brought very low: deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I.” David asks. “Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.” A lot of times we desire things but do not receive them because we do not ask.

David has a level of humility to say his persecutors are stronger than him. To have enemies stronger than you, you have to be willing to let the powers we have take that place instead of trying to handle it yourself.

precepts.text: When you do ask and receive not, it is because you ask amiss, to consume it upon your own lust.
precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

precepts.why:
“Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” When you do ask and receive not, it is because you ask amiss, to consume it upon your own lust. David asked for deliverance and for his soul to be brought out of prison so that he might praise the name of the Most High, not for his lusts.

You can ask the Lord for something and then do the opposite; when you pray you should put in the effort to make it happen. If you want a house, a wife, or a husband, you have to put in the work.

precepts.text: If any lack wisdom, let him ask of God who gives to all men liberally; but ask in faith, not wavering, for the Lord gives what He thinks you need, not simply whatever you asked for.
precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

precepts.why:
“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” Ask of God, who gives to all men liberally; but ask in faith, not wavering, for the Lord gives what he thinks you need, not simply whatever you asked for. David cried to his refuge and his portion in the land of the living, trusting the Most High to deal bountifully with him.

When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

precepts.text: God heareth not sinners; a man after the Lord's own heart is a man that keeps the commandments, and the Lord deals with those that are Israel and keep His commandments.
precepts.point: When we read our four chapters we should read to understand, seeing how the examples of our forefathers and foremothers can be used for us.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

precepts.why: “Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.” David could say “Attend unto my cry” because a man after the Lord’s own heart is a man that keeps the commandments. The Lord deals with those that are Israel and keep his commandments, and to them he deals bountifully, and the righteous compass them about.

points: A key point is that David pours out his complaint before the Lord and shows before Him his trouble. A lot of times Israel goes to the Lord when troubles are going on, when things are getting rough and going bad.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

points: When his spirit was overwhelmed within him: everybody has been to a point where things have been too much for them, too much to bear. Even so, David understands the Lord is his refuge, so you can have a hard time but you must keep your mind in the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

points: Verse 4 shows he could not handle it himself; he looked on his right hand and there was no man that would know him, no man cared for his soul.

note.label: Psalm 142: The Lord My Refuge and Portion

points: David calls the Lord his refuge and his portion in the land of the living. He is brought very low and asks to be delivered from persecutors that are stronger than he is.

David has a level of humility to say his persecutors are stronger than him. To have enemies stronger than you, you have to be willing to let the powers we have take that place instead of trying to handle it yourself.
